Hacker News #5

卡帕蒂鹈鹕

Karpathy’s Pelican

AI 作者 delichon 热度 583 回复 397 2026/08/02 12:05
打开原帖 打开外部链接 JSON

摘要

  • We're starting to leave the territory where you'd test an LLM by e.g. "create an svg of pelican on a bicycle". As one idea to generalize it, I was interested what Opus 5 would do if I gave it the first paragraph of the Lord of the Rings, a 1M token budget (~$10) and asked for three js render of it. Opus went off for ~2 hours and wrote 5500 lines of code that (procedurally) rendered the story. It's kind of janky but fun. But it's a bit mindboggling that the LLM has to place and orchestrate various polygon assets in (x,y,z) coordinates and write code that animates it all, and that it even does anything at all.
  • I also like this kind of examples because no one in their right mind would ever spend the time to write something this custom but LLMs have all the stamina and patience in the world, so it's an example where we go from "no one would ever do this" to "sure, why not, it's ~free". There might be a lot more. But I'm excited about creating hyper custom worlds that you can imagine dropping players into, e.g. here to participate in the LoTR story as a spectator NPC, or one of the characters, or etc. Something like an ephemeral GTA of X on demand.

命中 3 个 AI/科技关键词。

jmugan 2026/08/03 01:56
很多人都在这里发帖谈论最终产品有多糟糕，但这就是重点。模型已经超越了生成图像的范畴，发展成为一种新的基准，可以更好地揭示对物理世界的理解，我们可以使用这样的基准来衡量未来的进展。 （当然，它必须是定性/主观测量。）
A lot of people are posting here about how bad the end product is, but that is kind of the point. Models have moved beyond generating images to a new kind of benchmark that better exposes understanding of the physical world, and we can use benchmarks like this to measure future progress. (Of course, it will have to be a qualitative/subjective measurement.)

maxutility 2026/08/03 02:05
同意。一年前，鹈鹕基准测试很有趣，当时大多数模型都在挣扎，而一个好的鹈鹕则表明了一个异常有能力的模型。现在它已经饱和并且无趣了。

一个好的新基准应该有糟糕的开始性能，并且应该有很大的改进空间。这个基准也故意设置了难度，要求法学硕士通过空间推理和第一原理而不是现有的视频生成管道来开发动画。类似于一年前 SVG 生成在大多数型号中不再发行的情况。

Agree. The pelican benchmark was interesting a year ago when most models struggled and a good pelican indicated an unusually capable model. Now it’s saturated and uninteresting.

A good new benchmark should have awful performance to start and there should be a lot of headroom for improvement. This benchmark is also intentionally difficult and requires the LLM to develop the animation through spatial reasoning and first principals rather than existing video generation pipelines. Similar to how SVG generation was out of distribution for most models a year ago.

他们也非常擅长放置和创建场景等。我在 vulkan/glfw 中实现了一个级联阴影系统，然后将其反馈了带有 Peter Pannin 和痤疮斑点等的屏幕截图。

they are quite good also at placement and creating scenes etc. I had one implement a cascading shadow system in vulkan/glfw and just fed it back screenshots with peter pannin and acne spots etc.

it made a huge monstrosity first, 1500+ lines of shader code. Once it was happy with the result (it looked pretty good, almost blenders gamerenderer) it cleaned it up and a lot of debug code was removed. shrank it down to about 350 lines and made it much more readable.

this was something i didnt expect it to be able to do. create shaders, look at screenshots, fix em iteratively like that. multi modal debugging.

doginasuit 2026/08/03 10:18
为了帮助向我年迈的母亲解释人工智能，我说它就像一个距离太远而无法直接观察地球的行星上的外星智能体，它通过阅读几乎每一本书和网站了解到有关人类和我们世界的一切。你可以问它一个问题或做一些工作，它通常可以给出有用的响应，但如果它与物理世界相关，它永远无法直接判断其准确性，它只能根据你的判断进行工作。

考虑到这一限制，它仍然可以完成令人难以置信的事情。当它达不到要求时，它通常会以一种迷人的方式出现，如果你愿意以这种方式看待它的话。它反映了孩子对世界的理解，并非完全错误，只是不完整。

那些可能是蜜蜂或蝴蝶的飘动的立方体是我最喜欢的部分。

To help explain AI to my elderly mother, I said it is like an alien intelligence on a planet too far away to directly observe Earth, and everything it knows about humanity and our world it learned from reading just about every book and website. You can ask it a question or to do some work and it can often give a useful response but it can never directly judge its accuracy if it relates to the physical world, it has only your judgment to work with.

Given that limitation, it is incredible what it can still accomplish. And when it falls short, it is often in a charming way, if you are open to seeing it that way. It reflects something like a child's understanding of the world, not entirely wrong, just incomplete.

The fluttering cubes that might have been bees or butterflies were my favorite part.

Valakas_ 2026/08/03 14:06
这是对你母亲的一个很好的比喻，我喜欢它。我只想谈一小部分，那就是它的内容超出了我们的判断。它可以获取物理定律、公式以及我们当前所有的科学知识，这些知识通过与物理世界的互动而被证明是正确的。它可以根据已验证的理论创建一个（不完整的）世界模型。仅通过演绎和推理就可以走得很远。毕竟，我们在通过与物理世界的相互作用实际证明它们是正确的之前就已经提前创建了许多科学理论。因此，即使在它们被证明是正确的之前，它们就已经是正确的了。同样的情况也适用于法学硕士仅通过推理就能推断出的内容。

无论如何，这只是一个小点，可能仍然不会改变你所做的漂亮比喻。

That's a nice metaphor for your mother, i like it. I would just touch on one small part, which is that it has more than our judgement though. It has access to laws of physics, to formulas, to all our current scientific knowledge which we have shown to be correct by interacting with the physical world. It can create an (incomplete) model of the world based on verified theories already. Through deduction and reasoning alone it can get pretty far. After all, there's many scientific theories we created long in advance before we actually proved them to be correct through interaction with the physical world. So even before they were proved to be correct, they were already correct. Same can be applied to what LLM can infer through reasoning alone.

Anyway, just a small point which probably still wouldn't change the nice metaphor your made.
